display_name: National Insurance Law ss 342 and 348 and Schedule K: who is liable to pay insurance contributions and the employer's deduction from the wage; the maximum, minimum and disregarded income; and the income bounds per month, quarter and year for each kind of insured person

run.method: one agent, one session, no sub-agents, from BRIEF.md

depends_on.how: Not imported: the l4 binary resolves an IMPORT by bare module name beside the importing file, so IL-04's modules in the sibling directory are not found (NOTES.md section 8). IL-04's types A branch of insurance and A column of insured persons in Schedule J are declared again with the same names and constructors; IL-04's Schedule J column D amounts and s 334(a) threshold enter as inputs; IL-04's s 337 takes this row's s 348 result as its income input. NOTES.md section 6 lists what to join at IL-07.

language.note: Identifiers and comments are English (@lang en). Hebrew is quoted only in `-- src:N |` comments generated mechanically from line N of the deposited source by row IL-04's tools/srcquote.py (run by path, not copied), and in short runs that IL-04's tools/hebcheck.py checks occur verbatim in it.

source.authority: aid: unofficial Hebrew Wikisource consolidation, as amended at retrieval

published_figures.note: Figures the Law computes but does not print, taken from the National Insurance Institute's pages fetched 2026-10-06; URLs and sha256 in nii-il05-published-figures.l4 and NOTES.md section 7.

scope: Encoded: s 342(a), (b), (c)(1), (c)(2) (pension, age, police and prison officers, the employer's permission to reduce), (d) with its two definitions, (e1), (f)(1)-(2); s 348(a), (a1), (b), (c) (the power's test, and a decline where an order reaches), (d) (where its readings agree), (e) permanent and temporary texts; Schedule K in full, four items, maximum and minimum, per month, quarter and year, with 'quarter', 'minimum wage' and 'basic amount'. Inert: headings; s 342(e)(1)-(4) and (f)(3), powers whose regulations are not in the sources. Out of scope: Schedule K1 (only s 369 refers to it), and every provision outside the slice, each taken as an input with its citation (NOTES.md section 2).

years_answered.contribution periods: January 2026 on; earlier periods declined by name (s 342's text is from 1 January 2026 by the 2025 budget-year Law s 19(4) and s 21; this row answers with row IL-04)
years_answered.figures: 2026 from the Institute's published figures; 2027 on only when the caller supplies them
years_answered.s 348(e) temporary text: to 31.8.2026, and after it for one who began national-civic service before that day

expected_red.why: The source against itself: s 342(e)(3) and (e)(4) name column E of Schedule J for the rates of deduction, where the deduction is column D (2); s 342(c)(2) is made subject to s 245(b2), which is repealed (1). Findings about the source, not defects of the encoding: NOTES.md section 0, forks F10 and F22.

The independent tester's module, not edited by the encoder; its results are the same at 0.1.0 and 0.3.0. check.sh did not list it before 0.3.0 and so ran red; from 0.3.0 it is listed with its counts so that the run's exit status reflects them. NOTES.md 'Version 0.3.0'.

not_reviewed.note: No domain expert has read this encoding against the source. No independent test pass was run (the row was briefed as one session with no sub-agents); every expected value in the tests modules was worked out before it was asserted, by a computation over the source's figures and the Institute's printed figures that does not use this encoding.

forks.F1: Schedule K and s 348(a1) read the average wage calculated under s 2 (13,769 for 2026): s 2(b) applies 'for benefits and contributions', and every Institute figure checked fits it and not the s 1 figure.
forks.F2: Items 2-4 print no monthly figure; a month's is a third of the quarter's.
forks.F3: s 348(a1) is a deduction of up to 25% of the average wage, not all-or-nothing (the other reading is encoded beside it).
forks.F4: s 348(a1)'s sum is a month's; other periods with income not from work are declined.
forks.F5: s 348(d) as a deeming or a floor: answered only where both agree (income not above the item 3 minimum).
forks.F6: Schedule K item 3 is the classes s 348(d) and (e) name, whatever their income.
forks.F7: An employee or self-employed person also in a (d) or (e) class keeps item 1 or 2; where (d) or (e) would then disagree with (b), declined.
forks.F8: s 348(e)'s temporary text ends 31.8.2026; 'began before' is strict; a quarter or year across the date, for one who began on or after it, is declined.
forks.F9: s 342(c)(2): a month in which the age is reached after its first day, or the pension is payable for part of it, is declined.
forks.F10: s 342(c)(2)'s 'subject to s 245(b2)' has no effect: s 245(b2) is repealed (checked red).
forks.F11: Schedule K's minimum wage is the particular employee's (an input); for an employee with none given, item 1's minimum is declined.
forks.F12: s 342(c)(1)'s s 335 subsections are the branches maternity, accident injury, unemployment, disability, long-term care, senior citizens and survivors.
forks.F13: A deduction branch with no column D amount in the case is declined, not taken as 0.
forks.F14: The coordinated contributions of s 342(d) are s 342(c), (c)(2) included, on the total income as one employer's wage.
forks.F15: s 342(e1) when the other employer deducted more than the coordinated contributions: declined.
forks.F16: s 342(f)(2)'s 'lower than' is strict (nothing turns on it).
forks.F17: Whether s 348(b)'s minimum applies per employer or to the total under s 342(b): not modelled.
forks.F18: s 350(c) disapplies s 348(b) only, not (d) or (e).
forks.F19: The day an age is reached: the date of birth plus the months, keeping the day or the month's last day.
forks.F20: Schedule K's yearly figures are for a whole tax year; part years are not modelled.
forks.F21: 'the deduction in item 6 of Schedule J' is the unemployment branch's column D amount.
forks.F22: s 342(e)(3)-(4)'s 'column E' for deduction rates is not resolved (checked red; (e) decides nothing here).
forks.F23: (0.3.0) At the printed totals of Schedule J (row IL-04's fork F4, ruled 2026-10-07), a police or prison officer's deduction leaves out 'the deduction in item 6' as item 6's own amount: the total for the deduction branches together less the unemployment branch's amount.
forks.F24: (0.3.0) Row IL-04's fork F4, ruled 2026-10-07: s 342(c)(1)'s 'as in Schedule J' is read at the printed totals by default, an amount for the branches in which the employer deducts together that the caller gives as an argument (row IL-04's column D deduction at its default reading), the items' reading (the per-branch amounts summed) kept as the alternative. One switch: `section 342(c) — the reading of Schedule J this row takes where its totals row and its items differ`. The rules under their 0.1.0 names read the items.

repairs.ruling: Meng, 2026-10-07, relayed by the lead: Schedule J at its printed totals by default, the items' reading kept as the alternative (row IL-04's fork F4)
repairs.summary: v0.3.0 (from 0.1.0, aligned with row IL-04's version): the reading re-declared from IL-04; one switch for s 342(c); reading-aware forms of s 342(c), (c)(1), (c)(2), (d) and (e1) that take column D at the printed totals as an argument; the 0.1.0 names read the items; 4 tests re-pointed to the items by name, 11 added (NOTES.md, 'Version 0.3.0').
